principle: A gold target (cathode) at -300 to -600 V DC sits in argon at 0.1-1 Pa; the electric field sustains a glow-discharge plasma and Ar+ ions accelerated across the cathode sheath strike the target, knocking out (sputtering) neutral Au atoms by momentum transfer (Au sputter yield ~2.4 atoms/ion at 500 eV Ar+ [FACT: published typical range]). Permanent magnets behind the target trap secondary electrons in E×B drift loops (the 'racetrack'), densifying the plasma near the target so the discharge runs at 10-100x lower pressure and higher rate than a plain diode. Sputtered Au atoms fly ballistically (or with a few gas collisions) to the substrate and condense as a fine-grained polycrystalline film; adhesion is physical/atomic (no chemical bath), so an atomically clean substrate and usually a reactive interlayer (Ti/Cr/NiCr) are mandatory. Purely line-of-sight-dominated: the wire/part must be rotated or multi-cathode-exposed for wrap-around coverage.

substrates: stainless steel (304/316) - the natural PVD jewelry substrate, no barrier layer needed
mild/spring steel wire (works, but corrosion undercuts thin Au through pores; interlayer + thicker stack advised)
glass, ceramic, glazed porcelain (houseware) - PVD's unique advantage: NO conductivity required
plastics (with temperature limits ~<80-120 C substrate heating)
cutlery/spoons/cups (established industry: PVD 'gold' cutlery is usually TiN or TiN+Au flash)
applicability.steel_wire_notes: Anchor case. Steel wire coats well IF: (1) plasma/glow-discharge or ion pre-clean immediately before deposition, (2) 10-50 nm Ti or Cr adhesion interlayer sputtered first without breaking vacuum, (3) wire is rotated or passed through an inverted-cylindrical or dual-facing cathode arrangement for 360-degree coverage (single planar target coats only the facing side). Practical geometry for DIY: coat cut wire blanks or pre-formed rings on a rotating planetary fixture rather than continuous spool. Sputtered Au on stainless via Ti interlayer is the standard watch-industry decorative stack [FACT: standard industrial practice]. Heat load on thin wire is real: at decorative rates wire can reach 100-200 C unless dwell is limited or fixture heat-sinks it [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, medium].
applicability.non_conductive_notes: PVD is THE route for the owner's glass/ceramic houseware question: sputtering deposits on insulators directly (the substrate carries no current; only the target is the electrode). Glass needs solvent + plasma clean and a Ti/Cr interlayer for durable adhesion; bare Au on glass rubs off. Food-contact caveat: sputtered decorative layers on cutlery/cup rims are accepted industrially, but verify local food-contact regulation for interlayer metals (Ni-containing interlayers problematic for skin/food contact in EU) [FACT: EN 1811 nickel-release regime exists].
applicability.jewelry_thickness_classes: PVD gold in jewelry/watches is flash-to-thin class: 0.05-0.5 um typical decorative, 1 um is a premium watch-grade PVD gold; multi-micron sputtered Au is possible but slow and expensive vs electroplating. Common premium stack: hard base (TiN or CrN, 0.5-2 um, HV 2000+) + 0.05-0.2 um Au or Au-alloy top flash = scratch-resistant gold look with minimal gold [FACT: standard industrial decorative-PVD practice]. Marketing 'micron' classes (ASTM B488 / ISO 27874 thickness classes) are electrodeposit standards; use them only as thickness vocabulary, not as PVD compliance claims.

components.name: vacuum chamber
components.purpose: holds process environment at 1e-5 to 1e-3 mbar working range; base pressure to 1e-6 mbar
components.diy_notes: stainless or aluminum cylinder/cube, ISO-KF/CF flanged; DIY: 6-way CF/KF cross, stainless pot with Viton L-gasket lid, or surplus bell jar; internal volume small as possible (10-50 L) to shorten pump-down; all-metal or Viton seals, no PVC/rubber hose on high-vac side

components.name: roughing pump (rotary vane or scroll)
components.purpose: atmosphere -> ~1e-1 to 1e-2 mbar; backs the high-vac pump
components.diy_notes: 2-stage rotary vane 4-8 m3/h is the cheap workhorse (used units common); oil backstreaming managed with foreline trap; scroll pump is oil-free but 3-5x cost

components.name: high-vacuum pump (turbomolecular or oil diffusion)
components.purpose: reaches base pressure 1e-5 to 1e-6 mbar to strip water/O2 before deposition
components.diy_notes: small turbo (60-80 L/s, used ~$500-1500) is cleanest; oil diffusion pump is the classic cheap DIY route but backstreams oil (needs cold cap/baffle). Sputtering CAN run turbo-throttled or diffusion-baffled at process pressure; a gate/butterfly throttle valve protects the turbo from 0.5 Pa gas load

components.name: vacuum gauges (2 ranges)
components.purpose: Pirani/thermocouple gauge for rough range (1000 -> 1e-3 mbar) + Penning/cold-cathode or hot-ion gauge for high vac (1e-3 -> 1e-7 mbar); capacitance manometer or calibrated Pirani for setting Ar working pressure
components.diy_notes: used Pirani+Penning combo controllers are cheap; working-pressure repeatability matters more than absolute accuracy - mark your good operating point

components.name: magnetron cathode with Au target
components.purpose: water-cooled copper body, NdFeB magnet array (center pole + ring, balanced), target clamped or bonded on top, ground shield with 2-3 mm dark-space gap
components.diy_notes: 2-inch (50.8 mm) circular planar magnetron is the DIY/lab standard; buildable (published DIY designs exist) or bought ~$800-2500. Au target 2-inch x 0.125-inch is roughly 40-50 g gold - the single biggest capital-in-metal item; target utilization only 25-40% before racetrack burn-through on planar magnetrons [FACT: published typical], but eroded targets are refinable gold, not lost gold

components.name: DC power supply
components.purpose: 300-1000 V, current-regulated, 100-1000 W class, with arc suppression
components.diy_notes: lab MDX-class supplies used ~$500+; DIY from microwave-oven-transformer chains is done but arc handling is poor and lethal-voltage exposed - a real sputter supply is the recommended safety spend. Pulsed-DC not needed for pure Au (conductive target, no poisoning)

components.name: gas handling (Ar)
components.purpose: argon 99.999% (5N) via needle valve or mass-flow controller, 5-50 sccm typical into the chamber
components.diy_notes: welding-grade Ar (99.996+) works for decorative; needle valve + fixed pump throttle gives adequate pressure control for DIY; MFC is the upgrade

components.name: substrate fixture / rotation
components.purpose: holds wire blanks/rings 40-100 mm from target; single or dual-axis rotation for 360-degree coverage; optional shutter to hide substrate during target pre-sputter clean
components.diy_notes: rotary motion feedthrough (ferrofluidic or double-O-ring, KF25) + geared motor; a rotating cage/barrel ('sputter barrel') tumbles small parts like ring blanks - the PVD analog of barrel plating; shutter is a swiveling steel flap on a second rotary feedthrough

components.name: second magnetron OR multi-target holder (interlayer)
components.purpose: sputter Ti or Cr adhesion layer then Au WITHOUT breaking vacuum (breaking vacuum between layers ruins adhesion)
components.diy_notes: cheapest DIY alternative to a second magnetron: a two-piece target (Ti ring insert swap requires venting - bad) - honest answer is either two cathodes, or accept adhesion risk of Au-only on freshly plasma-cleaned stainless (works modestly for costume-grade, fails tape test on glass)

components.name: water cooling loop
components.purpose: removes 100-500 W from target; an uncooled Au target melts/debonds
components.diy_notes: closed loop with aquarium/PC-watercooling pump + radiator is adequate at <=300 W

components.name: wire-feed vacuum stages (continuous variant only)
components.diy_notes: see operation step 12 and diy_feasibility; NOT a rubber wiper seal

operation_sequence.action: substrate prep outside chamber: degrease (alkaline or solvent), rinse, IPA/acetone wipe or ultrasonic, dry; handle with gloves only
operation_sequence.parameters: ultrasonic 5-10 min in detergent then IPA; oil-free compressed air / N2 dry
operation_sequence.failure_watch: any fingerprint or drawing-lubricant residue = guaranteed delamination; wire drawing soap must be fully stripped

operation_sequence.action: load substrates on rotating fixture, verify target-substrate distance, close shutter over substrates, close chamber
operation_sequence.parameters: target-substrate distance 40-80 mm typical for 2-inch cathode [FACT: published typical range]
operation_sequence.failure_watch: hair/dust/flaking old deposits on fixture cause pinholes and arcs; wipe chamber shields

operation_sequence.action: rough pump: open roughing valve, pump chamber to crossover
operation_sequence.failure_watch: stalls above 1e-1 mbar = leak (Viton seal hair, scratched flange) or heavy outgassing (wet/dirty parts)

operation_sequence.action: crossover to high vac: close roughing, open gate/turbo valve, pump to base pressure
operation_sequence.parameters: target base pressure <=5e-5 mbar minimum for decorative, 1e-5 to 1e-6 mbar preferred [FACT: published typical range]; water is the dominant residual - mild bake or long pump improves adhesion
operation_sequence.failure_watch: base pressure plateau = virtual leak (trapped volume under screws) or real leak; poor base pressure -> oxidized interlayer -> adhesion failure

operation_sequence.action: admit Ar, throttle pump, set working pressure
operation_sequence.parameters: Ar 5-50 sccm; working pressure 3-10 mTorr (0.4-1.3 Pa) standard magnetron window; lower pressure = more energetic, denser film; higher = better step coverage, softer film [FACT: published typical range]
operation_sequence.failure_watch: pressure oscillation from needle-valve hunting; plasma won't ignite below ~1-2 mTorr on small magnetrons - raise pressure to strike, then reduce

operation_sequence.action: OPTIONAL but recommended for steel wire: substrate plasma clean (glow-discharge or RF/DC bias etch) with shutter closed or target off
operation_sequence.parameters: substrate biased -200 to -500 V in Ar 5-10 mTorr, 2-10 min; removes adsorbed water/oxide monolayer [FACT: standard practice; exact bias hardware varies]
operation_sequence.failure_watch: skipping this on steel/glass is the no.1 adhesion failure; over-etching heats and roughens fine wire

operation_sequence.action: target pre-sputter (burn-in) with shutter CLOSED: strike plasma on target, sputter 1-5 min to strip target surface oxide/contamination
operation_sequence.parameters: ignite at 10-20 mTorr if needed then settle to working point; run at process power
operation_sequence.failure_watch: arcing spikes on a new/contaminated target - let arc rate decay before opening shutter; persistent arcing = debonded target or flaking shield

operation_sequence.action: deposit adhesion interlayer (Ti or Cr cathode): open its shutter, sputter 10-50 nm
operation_sequence.parameters: Ti/Cr power density 5-10 W/cm2; 10-50 nm layer [FACT: published typical range]; NiCr 80/20 is the alternative where Cr metal handling is disliked; MUST be done at good base pressure - Ti getters O2, an oxidized Ti layer is glassy and weak
operation_sequence.failure_watch: vacuum break between interlayer and Au = start over; interlayer too thick (>100 nm Cr) adds brittleness for later forming

operation_sequence.action: deposit gold: switch/open Au cathode shutter, run to target thickness with fixture rotating
operation_sequence.parameters: Au target power density 5-15 W/cm2 water-cooled planar magnetron [FACT: published typical range]; on a 2-inch target that is ~100-300 W; discharge ~350-550 V, 0.2-0.8 A; rate at 50-70 mm distance roughly 0.5-3 nm/s => ~6-35 min per 1 um line-of-sight, and 2-4x longer effective on rotating wire (only part of each rotation faces the target) [ESTIMATE: handbook-range scaled, medium-high]
operation_sequence.duration: flash 0.1 um: 1-7 min; 0.5 um: 5-35 min (line-of-sight equivalent)
operation_sequence.failure_watch: arcs eject droplets (spits) = visible defects; substrate overheating tints/softens film; rate drift as racetrack deepens - log kWh per um

operation_sequence.action: ramp down: shutter closed, power off, Ar off, let target cool under vacuum 5-10 min
operation_sequence.parameters: cool below ~60 C before venting (hot Au/Ti oxidizes and fresh film stains)
operation_sequence.failure_watch: venting a hot chamber = discolored film and oxidized target face

operation_sequence.action: vent with dry N2 or Ar (preferred over room air), open, unload with gloves, inspect
operation_sequence.parameters: vent through filter; slow vent (>30 s) so films/foils don't get blasted
operation_sequence.failure_watch: fast humid-air vent drives water into every surface = next pump-down 3x longer

operation_sequence.action: CONTINUOUS WIRE-FEED VARIANT (honest treatment). The owner's sketch - wire running through a thick rubber seal in the chamber wall - does NOT work as primary vacuum containment: a sliding elastomer on moving wire either leaks (any gap or wire-diameter variation admits a huge gas load at 1 atm differential) or grips (abrades the wire, shreds the seal, and on the exit side scratches the fresh soft Au coating). What industry actually does, in order of prevalence: (a) IN-VACUUM REEL-TO-REEL - pay-off and take-up spools both live INSIDE the chamber; wire is coated spool-to-spool in a batch pump-down; no moving atmospheric feedthrough at all; this is the standard for sputter-metallized wire/fiber and the correct answer at this scale [FACT: standard industrial practice]; (b) DIFFERENTIAL PUMPING for true air-to-air lines: the wire passes through a series of 3-5 small chambers connected by close-fitting orifices/tubes only slightly larger than the wire (clearance ~0.1-0.5 mm); each stage has its own pump; each orifice stage drops pressure ~2-4 orders of magnitude, so atmosphere -> rough -> medium -> high vacuum in stages; nothing touches the wire or the coating [FACT: standard technique in continuous vacuum web/wire lines and accelerator physics]; capital and pump count make this an industrial, not DIY, build; (c) load-lock spool exchange as the middle path - coat spool-to-spool but exchange spools through a small load-lock so the main chamber stays under vacuum between runs
operation_sequence.parameters: orifice conductance sets stage pressure ratio; per-stage pumps sized to orifice gas load; wire speed in industrial lines set so dwell under the cathode(s) delivers target thickness [UNKNOWN - needs line-specific engineering, not a handbook constant]
operation_sequence.failure_watch: rubber-wiper designs additionally pump elastomer particulate and outgassing straight into the deposition zone - film contamination even before the leak problem

solutions.solution_name: process consumables: sputtering media (no wet bath - this is a dry process; 'solutions' here = consumable media)
solutions.purpose: sustain the discharge and supply the deposit

composition.role: inert sputtering ion source; sets working pressure 3-10 mTorr
composition.hazard_class: compressed inert gas - asphyxiant in confined space, pressurized cylinder [FACT]

composition.role: deposit source (cathode); 25-40% utilized before replacement on planar magnetron, remainder refinable
composition.hazard_class: not hazardous as bulk metal; fine sputter dust on shields is a valuable-scrap, not toxic, concern [FACT]

composition.typical_range: alloy per desired karat color (e.g. rose = Au-Cu rich)
composition.role: deposit color/karat follows target composition approximately (sputter yields of components differ slightly; steady-state film tracks target) [FACT: sputtering of alloys - steady-state stoichiometry transfer is textbook]
composition.tag: [FACT: published principle]; exact color recipes [UNKNOWN - needs supplier TDS]

composition.role: reactive adhesion layer bonding Au to steel oxide/glass; Cr slightly better on glass, Ti more benign, NiCr adds tarnish barrier
composition.hazard_class: Ti/Cr metal targets not hazardous as solids; Cr sputter dust - avoid inhalation; Ni-containing layers: skin-sensitizer relevance for jewelry (EN 1811 nickel release) [FACT]

composition.role: dry venting keeps chamber walls dry, protects hot fresh films

operating_window.temperature_C: substrate nominally unheated; self-heating 50-200 C at decorative rates; target water-cooled <50 C face-body [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, medium-high]
operating_window.current_density_A_dm2: expressed as target POWER DENSITY: 5-15 W/cm2 Au on cooled planar magnetron [FACT: published typical range]
operating_window.voltage: DC 300-600 V discharge at 3-10 mTorr Ar [FACT: published typical range]
operating_window.agitation: substrate rotation 5-30 rpm single/planetary, or barrel tumbling for small parts (replaces bath agitation)
operating_window.deposition_rate: 0.5-3 nm/s line-of-sight at 100-300 W, 50-70 mm throw => ~6-35 min per um static, 2-4x that on rotating wire [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, medium-high]
operating_window.anode: grounded chamber + ground shield are the anode; substrate floats or is biased (no consumable anode - the TARGET is the consumable cathode)

solutions.maintenance: no bath chemistry to maintain - maintenance = vacuum hygiene: strip/replace or glass-bead-blast shields when deposits flake (flakes cause arcs and pinholes); collect Au-bearing shield strip and spent targets for refining (30-60% of purchased gold ends up on shields/racetrack scrap - refine it, it is not lost); replace foreline oil per pump hours; leak-check O-rings; log base-pressure trend as chamber health metric; target replacement at racetrack ~70-80% depth

prep_chain_required: 1. strip wire-drawing lubricant / oils: alkaline ultrasonic or solvent degrease - WHY: PVD has zero tolerance for organics; there is no bath to dissolve them and the plasma clean only removes monolayers
2. mechanical finish BEFORE coating (polish/tumble to final luster) - WHY: PVD replicates surface topography exactly; a 0.1-0.5 um film hides nothing; premium look = premium pre-polish
3. final solvent rinse (IPA) + dry, gloves-only handling - WHY: fingerprint salts/oils = delamination spots
4. IN-VACUUM plasma/ion pre-clean - WHY: removes adsorbed water and native oxide monolayers minutes before deposition; the only 'pickle' PVD has
5. Ti/Cr/NiCr interlayer without vacuum break - WHY: Au does not bond chemically to steel oxide or glass; the reactive interlayer does; also blocks Fe out-diffusion staining

NOTE vs electroplating chain: NO pickle, NO strike, NO nickel underplate bath, NO hydrogen embrittlement risk (no cathodic hydrogen) - a genuine PVD advantage for spring-steel wire [FACT: no aqueous H source]

deposit_properties.purity_karat: film purity = target purity: 99.9%+ Au (24k look) from pure target; colored karat looks via alloy targets or Au-flash-over-TiN [FACT]
deposit_properties.hardness_HV: sputtered pure Au ~80-150 HV (fine grain makes it harder than annealed bulk gold ~25 HV and comparable to soft electroplated Au 60-90 HV) [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, medium]; scratch resistance of the PRODUCT comes from the stack: TiN/CrN undercoat 2000+ HV with Au flash is the industry premium-scratch-resistant answer [FACT: standard decorative PVD practice]
deposit_properties.thickness_per_pass: flash 0.05-0.2 um per run typical decorative; 0.5-1 um watch-premium; multi-um possible but time/cost scales linearly - electroplating wins economically above ~1 um [FACT: published industry positioning]
deposit_properties.color_control: set by target composition (alloy targets) or by undercoat (TiN gives brassy gold tone under thin Au); NOT tunable per-run like a plating bath - one target = one color; reactive tricks (TiN color via N2 ratio) apply to the nitride undercoat, not to Au itself
deposit_properties.ductility_forming_notes: CRITICAL for plate-then-form: pure sputtered Au is ductile and a 0.1-0.5 um Au film on steel wire survives modest forming strain (bending a 1 mm wire around a >=8-10 mm mandrel, outer-fiber strain ~5-10%, is at the edge - expect microcracking of the INTERLAYER first: Ti/Cr layers and especially any TiN/CrN hard undercoat are brittle and craze at ~1-2% strain, then the crack pattern prints through the Au) [ESTIMATE: thin-film mechanics handbook reasoning, medium]. Practical verdict: FORM FIRST, COAT SECOND. PVD's line-of-sight nature also under-coats the inner curve of a pre-bent ring unless rotated well - so the correct product flow is: cut + form ring blanks -> polish -> rack/barrel -> sputter. Hot re-forming after coating is worse, not better: above ~150-250 C Au interdiffuses with Cr/Ni interlayers and with steel, dulling color and killing adhesion [ESTIMATE: published diffusion behavior, medium-high]

testing_acceptance.standard_class: ISO 3497 / ASTM B568 class (XRF coating thickness)
testing_acceptance.acceptance: meets stated class, e.g. flash >=0.05 um or 'micron' >=1.0 um at defined points; XRF is non-destructive and the jewelry-trade norm

testing_acceptance.standard_class: ASTM B571 class (bend, tape, burnish for metallic coatings)
testing_acceptance.acceptance: no peel with pressure-sensitive tape after cross-hatch; for wire: wrap around mandrel of product-relevant diameter, no flaking (cracking of hard undercoat noted separately)

testing_acceptance.standard_class: Taber or rubbing-cloth cycles per retailer spec class; no single jewelry ISO
testing_acceptance.acceptance: no base-metal show-through after agreed cycles [UNKNOWN - acceptance count needs the owner's market spec]

testing_acceptance.standard_class: ISO 9227 NSS class; ISO 12870-style artificial perspiration for skin-contact goods
testing_acceptance.acceptance: no red rust from steel substrate at e.g. 24-96 h NSS for the chosen stack [ESTIMATE: typical decorative spec range, medium]

testing_acceptance.test: nickel release (if Ni/NiCr in stack, skin contact)
testing_acceptance.acceptance: <0.5 ug/cm2/week for prolonged skin contact items (EU) [FACT: regulatory limit]

testing_acceptance.standard_class: trade practice; ferroxyl-type porosity indicator class for steel substrates
testing_acceptance.acceptance: no spits, stains, rainbow (thin) zones, or porosity indications on face surfaces

defects_and_remedies.defect: film peels at tape test / flakes at bend
defects_and_remedies.cause: organics or oxide under film (skipped plasma clean, poor base pressure, vacuum break before Au, no interlayer)
defects_and_remedies.remedy: verify base pressure <=5e-5 mbar, add/lengthen in-situ plasma etch, deposit Ti/Cr interlayer in same pump-down

defects_and_remedies.defect: dull / brown / rainbow film instead of rich gold
defects_and_remedies.cause: film too thin (interference colors <~40 nm), or contaminated plasma (air leak, oil backstreaming), or overheated substrate
defects_and_remedies.remedy: fix leak (He or alcohol leak-check), add foreline trap/baffle, increase thickness past 80-100 nm, reduce power or dwell

defects_and_remedies.cause: target arcing: oxidized or debonded target, flaking shields, too-high power density
defects_and_remedies.remedy: pre-sputter longer with shutter closed, clean/blast shields, check target bonding and cooling, lower power, use supply with arc suppression

defects_and_remedies.defect: one-sided coating on wire, bare inner curves on rings
defects_and_remedies.remedy: planetary/barrel rotation, dual opposed cathodes, slow rotation relative to deposition time (many revolutions per run)

defects_and_remedies.cause: fresh soft Au dragged over guides/seals; rubber wiper seal abrading exit wire
defects_and_remedies.remedy: abandon wiper seals; in-vacuum reel-to-reel with large-radius polished/PTFE-lined guides touching wire minimally; interleave spool with paper only after full cool-down

defects_and_remedies.defect: steel shows red rust through coating in weeks
defects_and_remedies.cause: pinholes in thin PVD stack over mild steel - galvanic cell, Au is cathodic to steel and ACCELERATES pitting at pores [FACT: galvanic series]
defects_and_remedies.remedy: use stainless wire (the clean fix), or thicken stack / add dense CrN or NiCr barrier, or e-coat/topcoat lacquer for houseware

defects_and_remedies.defect: pump-down takes hours, base pressure drifts up
defects_and_remedies.cause: water-soaked chamber (humid vent), virtual leaks, aging O-rings, pump oil degraded
defects_and_remedies.remedy: dry-N2 venting, minimize open time, mild chamber bake or heat-lamp, vent-and-replace O-rings annually, change roughing oil

defects_and_remedies.cause: rate drift with racetrack erosion, pressure setpoint drift, different substrate loading (heat)
defects_and_remedies.remedy: run to time x power (kWh) recipe not just time; log target hours; keep fixture load constant; requalify recipe after target change

cost_drivers: capital: pumps + chamber + magnetron(s) + supply = realistic DIY-refurb floor ~USD 3-8k, decent used lab coater 10-25k, industrial inline wire system 100k+ [ESTIMATE: market-range, medium]

gold target inventory: ~45 g Au locked in each 2-inch target (~USD 5k at 2026 prices) with only 25-40% direct utilization - cash tied up, though scrap is refinable at 97-99% recovery minus refining fee

cycle time is pump-down-dominated: 30-90 min overhead per batch regardless of parts count -> economics demand maximizing parts per pump-down (barrel/rack density), which is exactly why industry batches spools in-vacuum rather than air-to-air feed
electricity + Ar are minor (a few USD per run); labor per batch and rework rate dominate variable cost at DIY scale
second cathode (interlayer) nearly doubles cathode+supply capital but removes the largest scrap driver (adhesion failure)
thickness: PVD cost scales ~linearly with microns; above ~0.5-1 um electroplating is cheaper per micron - PVD's sweet spot is flash color + hard-undercoat scratch resistance, not heavy gold weight

hazards: lethal DC voltage: 300-1000 V supplies at ampere-class current - contact is electrocution risk [FACT]
implosion/vacuum: bell jars and thin-wall chambers can implode; glass shrapnel [FACT]
compressed gas cylinders (Ar, N2): asphyxiation in unventilated rooms, cylinder projectile risk [FACT]

UV and some soft X-ray emission from the discharge through viewports at high voltage (minor at <1 kV, real above several kV - not a magnetron issue at normal settings but a DIY-overvolt issue) [FACT: physics; magnitude at <1 kV is low]
strong NdFeB magnet assemblies: crush/pinch, pacemaker exclusion zone [FACT]
Cr/Ni-containing dusts from shield cleaning: sensitizer/inhalation hazard - wet-clean or HEPA [FACT]
controls: interlocked HV: supply enable tied to chamber-closed and water-flow switches; all HV leads shielded; one-hand rule when probing
polycarbonate implosion guard around any glass chamber section; use metal chambers where possible
cylinder chained, regulator + flashback-free inert setup, room ventilation / O2 monitor if small room
dark UV-filtering viewport glass; do not stare at plasma through plain glass for long periods
wet-wipe or HEPA-vac shield deposits; gloves + FFP3 when bead-blasting shields
water-flow interlock on target cooling (a burst target is both a HV and a gold-loss event)
safety.waste: essentially benign vs plating: no cyanide, no metal-laden rinse water, no acids. Waste streams = spent pump oil (recycle as used oil), Au-bearing shield strip + spent targets (ASSET - send to refiner), occasional solvent from degreasing (flammable-waste container). This near-zero-effluent profile is PVD's biggest regulatory advantage over any gold bath for a home/small shop [FACT]

diy_feasibility.verdict: GENUINELY FEASIBLE at batch scale for a serious builder - the hardest DIY vacuum-deposition process is NOT this one; small-magnetron gold sputtering is a well-trodden amateur/lab path. The continuous air-to-air wire-feed version is NOT DIY-feasible; the in-vacuum reel-to-reel or rack-batch version is the honest route to 'mass, not volume' throughput.
diy_feasibility.minimum_viable_setup: 10-30 L stainless chamber (KF/CF), 2-stage rotary vane 4-8 m3/h + used 60-80 L/s turbo (or baffled diffusion pump), Pirani+Penning gauging, ONE bought 2-inch magnetron with Au target + ONE with Ti (or accept single-cathode compromise initially on stainless only), 300-500 W DC supply with arc suppression, needle-valve Ar from a welding cylinder, rotating fixture on a KF25 rotary feedthrough, closed-loop water cooling. Budget floor ~USD 4-8k excluding the ~USD 5k gold target metal value. Skills required: vacuum plumbing/leak hunting, HV discipline, patience with pump-down.
diy_feasibility.hard_limits: 1) line-of-sight physics - complex/hollow shapes and long continuous wire need rotation hardware or multiple cathodes, never solvable with 'more time'; 2) thickness economics - do not chase multi-micron gold with sputtering, hybridize (PVD hard undercoat + electroplated gold, or PVD-only flash class); 3) sliding rubber seals on moving wire cannot hold sputtering vacuum - differential-pumped orifice trains are industrial-grade builds (3-5 pumped stages), so DIY continuous = spools inside the chamber; 4) batch overhead (pump-down) sets a floor of ~1-2 h per batch - throughput comes from fixture density, not line speed; 5) plate-then-form is materials-limited: interlayers/hard undercoats crack at low strain - form first, coat second.
